transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-02
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes (recording may be slightly longer)
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Aerolith CTO), Jordan Lee (Eng Mgr), Priya Singh (Head of Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Aerolith is evaluating Redwood for an internal LLM assistant and document-search features, initial interest in hosted quickstart but long-term possibility of Dedicated/VPC because of compliance.
- Primary asks: time-to-first-token for hosted free credits, perf for 512-2k token contexts, SOC2/KMS/VPC details, pricing for pilot and reserved capacity.
- Next steps: send quickstart + trial creds, schedule benchmarking, share security docs, follow-up security review.

[00:00] Alex Rivera: hey everyone thanks for joining. um quick intros \u000e2\u00128\u00196 i'm alex from redwood, ae on this acct, with samir our solutions eng.
[00:12] Maya Chen: hi all, maya here, cto at aerolith, thanks for setting this up. we have jordan and priya on too.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: yep thanks alex. trying to keep this short we want to understand quickstart path and what it'd take to run some benchmarks.
[00:25] Samir Patel: awesome, that sounds good. i'll give a quick run through of the plg quickstart flow \u000e2\u00128\u00196 how to get to first token, the free credits experience, and then we can talk about dedicated/private for later.
[00:36] Priya Singh: also want to cover security \u000e2\u00128\u00196 we have strict data residency and key management reqs so would like to know when the private option would be necessary.
[00:44] Alex Rivera: totally makes sense. quick agenda: 1) quickstart and time-to-first-token, 2) free credits and trial limits, 3) performance notes (latency/throughput), 4) security and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private), 5) next steps. sound ok?
[00:58] Maya Chen: yes.

[02:10] Samir Patel: so on quickstart \u000e2\u00128\u00196 typical flow is sign up, verify email, create API key in Console, run quickstart curl or our SDK. most engineers are at first token in like 5-10 minutes. we provision free hosted credits that are visible in the console, they can be used immediately.
[02:32] Jordan Lee: 5-10 minutes sounds nice. is that for a basic text-gen or for embedding workloads too?
[02:38] Samir Patel: both \u000e2\u00128\u00196 the SDK examples include text gen and embeddings. embeddings are batch-y so depends on size but first-run tokens are immediate. note that large-batch embedding runs will be queued or batched to optimize cost.
[02:50] Maya Chen: what about streaming? we need streaming responses for our chat assistant.
[02:55] Samir Patel: yep supported \u000e2\u00128\u00196 streaming via eventstream or websocket in SDK; latency's usually dominated by model and seq length.

[04:05] Priya Singh: when you say hosted credits, are those tied to an account with us storing data? what's retained?
[04:12] Alex Rivera: good question. the hosted trial credits sit on Redwood hosted plane and by default we retain logs for 30 days for debugging but you can opt out; for sensitive data we recommend using masked logging or the private deployment. we'll share the retention settings and the audit log options.
[04:30] Priya Singh: do you have SOC2 and ISO certs? and KMS integration?
[04:34] Samir Patel: yes, SOC 2 Type II in our security pack, we support customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated and Private, and we can integrate with AWS KMS or GCP KMS depending on the private deployment. we'll send the security doc link. (link shared: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack)

[06:00] Jordan Lee: switching to perf \u000e2\u00128\u00196 our primary workload is short chat turns ~200 tokens but some routes use up to 2k tokens. what's p95 latency on hosted vs dedicated?
[06:10] Samir Patel: for small models and short seqs hosted p95 is typically sub-200ms for 128 token completion on GPU-optimized runtime; for 2k tokens it depends on model variant and quantization. Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor effects and gives more predictable throughput \u000e2\u00128\u00196 we can target a p95 SLA with reserved pools.
[06:34] Maya Chen: can you quantify that? like numbers for a 2k token completion on a 70B model?
[06:40] Samir Patel: rough ballpark without benchmark: 70B unquantized on sequence 2k could be multiple seconds \u000e2\u00128\u00196 say 2-6s depending on hardware; quantized variants or smaller models can be sub-second to couple seconds. that said, we recommend a benchmark with your prompt set \u000e2\u00128\u00196 we can provision sample runs on hosted trial or run on a dedicated bench instance.

[08:05] Alex Rivera: important tradeoffs \u000e2\u00128\u00196 hosted is fastest to get started and no infra ops; dedicated gives predictability and isolation; private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulated data and gives full control incl. KMS and audit logs. most customers start hosted to validate and then move to dedicated for scale or private for compliance.

[09:10] Maya Chen: for pricing \u000e2\u00128\u00196 curious about overage or reserved pricing. we have a small pilot (~$10k mo) then likely expand.
[09:18] Alex Rivera: we have usage-based for hosted, and reserved contracts for Dedicated. i'll send a pilot pricing sheet that maps usage to expected cost; also we provide batching and caching suggestions to reduce token costs \u000e2\u00128\u00196 that's part of Redwood Optimize.

[10:25] Jordan Lee: do you support pinning model versions and automatic fallbacks? we want to avoid regressing quality mid-run.
[10:32] Samir Patel: yes, the console supports model pinning and rollouts; you can set canary and automatic fallback to older variants or cheaper models if latency spikes.

[12:00] Priya Singh: for our security review we'll need network diagrams, data flow, and audit logs detail. do you do on-prem installs?
[12:08] Samir Patel: we do a Redwood Private deployment for on-prem or VPC-connected control plane; it includes options for HSM/KMS and enhanced logging. we'll add the on-prem package info to the docs we send.

[13:15] Maya Chen: what about tokenization and pricing for embedding vs text \u000e2\u00128\u00196 embeddings are per-vector?
[13:22] Alex Rivera: embeddings are billed per-embedding unit (vector) and text is per-token; we'll include examples in the pricing sheet. also recommend using prefix caching for common prompts to cut costs.

[14:40] Jordan Lee: the quickstart \u000e2\u00128\u00196 can we self-serve the trial for our org or does it require an AE?
[14:46] Samir Patel: self-serve for the hosted quickstart. AE helps with pilot scoping, security, and dedicated. We'll provision trial credits via the console as soon as you sign up; Alex can also send a promo link that auto-applies credits to your account.

[16:05] Maya Chen: ok we'd like to get devs to try this this week. what's the flow for setting up an org with single sign-on?
[16:12] Alex Rivera: SSO via SAML/Okta is available; can be enabled on your org's console. for pilot we often start with email-based accounts and then enable SSO when moving to dedicated/private.

[17:00] Priya Singh: data residency \u000e2\u00128\u00196 our EU data must stay in EU region, do you support region pinning for hosted?
[17:05] Samir Patel: yes region pinning is supported; hosted has regional endpoints (us/eu/apac) and you can pin routes to EU-only. for stricter sovereignty we recommend Private.

[18:30] Jordan Lee: sample integration \u000e2\u00128\u00196 we plan a chat assistant + document retrieval chain with embeddings. any architecture recommendations?
[18:38] Samir Patel: typical pattern: document ingestion -> embedding store (we integrate with vector DBs or you can store embeddings in your infra) -> retrieval -> prompt assembly -> Redwood API for generation. use steady-state batching for embeddings and prefix/KV caching for chat to lower tokens. we can share a reference diagram.

[20:00] Maya Chen: what about rate limits and throttling? we get spikes sometimes.
[20:07] Samir Patel: we have per-route quotas and rate limits; can request higher limits for pilot and dedicated has guaranteed throughput. we also support burst policies.

[21:40] Alex Rivera: quick question \u000e2\u00128\u00196 are there any blockers like procurement or CISO approvals we should be aware of to get the pilot started?
[21:49] Maya Chen: procurement will need a statement of work for the pilot and security will want the doc pack. pricing is fine for pilot.

[23:05] Priya Singh: also need data deletion guarantees and contract language for data processing.
[23:11] Alex Rivera: we can provide standard DPA clauses and data deletion options; for private deployments you can keep all data in your env. we'll surface the legal docs.

[24:30] Jordan Lee: for benchmarks \u000e2\u00128\u00196 we can share 50 sample prompts and desired latencies; can you run tests and give p50/p95 numbers?
[24:38] Samir Patel: yes, if you share prompt set and sample payloads we can run a bench on hosted trial or on a dedicated bench instance and return p50/p95 and throughput. we'll include a test plan in the follow-up.

[26:15] Maya Chen: curious about model catalog \u000e2\u00128\u00196 do you host open models and also allow custom weights?
[26:22] Samir Patel: we host a curated catalog of open models and Redwood-verified profiles. you can bring custom models for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we also support partner models.

[28:00] Jordan Lee: what's the onboarding story for engineers \u000e2\u00128\u00196 do you have SDKs, sample apps?
[28:06] Alex Rivera: yes SDKs in python/js, quickstart templates and a sample chat app repo. we also have a one-click quickstart in the console to provision creds and run sample requests.

[29:35] Priya Singh: can we get a copy of the quickstart so our engs can follow offline?
[29:39] Alex Rivera: yes i'll email a dev quickstart link and the promo creds.

[31:00] Samir Patel: small note on observability \u000e2\u00128\u00196 Console gives per-route token cost breakdown, trace hooks, and example evals. Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization to lower cost while maintaining quality.

[32:10] Maya Chen: for our pilot we plan 3 engineers to run tests over two weeks. how do limits work for a shared org?
[32:18] Alex Rivera: org-level quotas can be set; we'll provision trial credits and temporarily raise quotas for the pilot if needed.

[33:45] Jordan Lee: any gotchas with websocket streaming and reconnects?
[33:50] Samir Patel: reconnection logic is standard; we publish sample code. for high availability use our SDK streaming helpers and implement resume tokens.

[35:10] Priya Singh: i'm also checking compliance \u000e2\u00128\u00196 does Redwood provide external pen-test reports or we need to run our own?
[35:18] Samir Patel: we can share third-party pen test summaries and provide contact for our security team. for bespoke assessments we can coordinate a scoping call.

[36:40] Alex Rivera: ok recap and next steps \u000e2\u00128\u00196 we'll: 1) send quickstart guide + trial credits link, 2) share security pack (SOC2, KMS options, network diagrams), 3) Samir will prepare bench test plan, 4) schedule 30-min benchmark session next week.

[37:05] Maya Chen: that works. can we also get pricing ballpark for a $10k/mo pilot and a committed 12-month reserved capacity number?
[37:14] Alex Rivera: yes i'll include pilot pricing and reserved options in the follow-up.

[38:30] Jordan Lee: timeline-wise we'd like to have pilot running by 2026-10-07, and security call by 2026-10-09.
[38:40] Priya Singh: yes.

[40:00] Samir Patel: noted. i'll draft the bench plan and sample scripts.

[40:10] Alex Rivera: thanks everyone. i'll send the materials and set a Doodle for the benchmark slot.

[41:20] Maya Chen: thanks alex, samir. appreciate it.

[41:25] Jordan Lee: thanks.

[41:28] Priya Singh: bye.
